statement: Product-level net-price variant (US CAR-T revenue at the price in force: implied CMS ASP where the file gives it, else the year's WAC, no factor; ex-US revenue at launch list times 0.76) for the five CAR-Ts with an ASP series and a US split (Yescarta, Tecartus, Breyanzi, Abecma, Carvykti) gives 72 to 83 percent of the main series' cumulative central counts (Yescarta 24,414 vs 29,589; Carvykti 9,822 vs 13,404; Breyanzi 8,336 vs 11,651; Abecma 4,620 vs 5,825; Tecartus 5,024 vs 6,279). Against Kite's four disclosed cumulative floors (2,500 Yescarta-only at end 2019; more than 11,000, 17,700 and 25,000 Kite patients at December 2022, January 2024 and January 2025) the variant recovers 81, 85, 90 and 87 percent, below every floor, while the class-factor series recovers 103, 104, 110 and 106 percent. US net equals list (F030) therefore does not carry to the worldwide count: ex-US prices below 0.76 of US launch list, free and trial doses, or list-price increases before the ASP series begins absorb the difference. The class factor stays the primary series (D011 confirmed).

statement: Systematic post-approval event table for the 43 cohort products: 151 rows (111 usable) from 102 agent-sourced disclosures, the seed list, the cohort's EU withdrawals and the disclosure statements. Counting retreats after first approval (discontinuation or withdrawal, shipment pause or label restriction, restructuring or impairment attributed to the product, sponsor exit, going private; the 2024 class-wide CAR-T boxed warning and priority-review-voucher sales excluded; asset sales reported separately), 22 of 43 products have at least one retreat event, at a median 20.5 months from first approval (range 0.8, Skysona, to 85.4, Luxturna's Roche restructuring). By class: AAV 6 of 11 (median 31.8 months; 4 withdrawn anywhere: Glybera, Beqvez, Roctavian, Elevidys in the EU), ex vivo lentiviral or retroviral 5 of 7 (15.4 months; Zynteglo and Skysona withdrawn), autologous CAR-T 2 of 7 (Abecma's sponsor spin-off and Aucatzyl's restructuring; none withdrawn), other classes 9 of 18. Ten products were withdrawn somewhere; 17 saw their sponsor acquired or the asset change hands; 6 were sold or licensed after approval. Products first approved in 2022 or later show 12 retreats among 27 against 10 among 16 approved earlier, with shorter follow-up. Stated amounts include Roctavian charges USD 240m and 60m, Elevidys restructuring 400m, Zynteglo and Skysona wind-down 160m, Kite acquisition 11.9bn, AveXis 8.7bn, Spark 4.8bn, Juno 9.0bn.

statement: Landscape projection 2027 to 2036 (D013). Backcast: the industry pipeline at end-2019 (sponsor-level programme proxy, S06 rates, measured clinical-stage distributions) predicts 30 (24 to 35) approvals in the five projected classes for 2020 to 2025 against 16 realised; per-class calibration (CAR-T 0.45, AAV 0.50, lentiviral 1.0, CRISPR 0.50, in vivo 0.58) brings the backcast to 16 (12 to 21) with every year inside the 10th to 90th band. Forecast: 54 (46 to 63) first approvals of genetic products 2027 to 2036 (CAR-T 17, AAV 15, lentiviral 8, CRISPR 2, in vivo editing and LNP 2, other vectors 10 at the historical rate), front-loaded at 10 a year in 2028 and 2029 and falling to 2 to 3 a year by 2033 as the phase-2 stock (59 CAR-T, 37 AAV industry programmes) clears. Patients treated per year worldwide: about 17,000 in 2027, 25,000 (17,000 to 42,000) in 2031, 37,000 (22,000 to 66,000) in 2036, CAR-T four fifths throughout (US 5,300 to 11,600; Europe 6,100 to 14,800); one-time gene therapies about 3,700 a year worldwide by 2036. Products with funded access by 2036 (median): US 60, Germany 59, Italy 51, France 41, England 37, Australia 37, Canada 33, driven by each system's share of approvals ever funded (0.57 to 0.91) more than by its lag. Compressing every access lag to the best observed adds 3 percent to 2036 volume. CAR-T centre capacity keeps pace only at the observed 12 percent a year growth in centres; frozen at 160 US centres the US ceiling is about 6,000 a year at German throughput.
